chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you buy your sacrificial animal, face the Qiblah with it, and slaughter it or sacrifice it.
And say: 'I have turned my face toward Him who originated the heavens and the earth, upright, and I am not of the polytheists.'
Surely my Prayer and my sacrifice and my life and my death are (all) for Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
There is no associate for Him; and with that I am Commanded, and I am from the Muslims.
O Allah, from You and for You. In the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, accept from me.
Then move the knife and do not break its bones until it dies.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and actions when slaughtering an animal for sacrifice in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the Sunnah of slaughtering the Hady for Hajj, emphasizing the recitation of Surah Al-An'am verses 162-163 as a declaration of monotheism and exclusive devotion to Allah. It highlights the practical etiquette of facing the Qiblah and ensuring a swift death by keeping the knife sharp, reflecting the Prophet's tradition as transmitted through the Imams. The inclusion of these specific verses underscores the theological link between ritual sacrifice and the concept of 'Hanif' (upright monotheist).
